hints: Focus on where the H can be removed from, elimination needs a H on a carbon next to the C-Br carbon.
Draw out 2-bromobutane as $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and notice C1 and C3 both have H atoms next to C2.
Remove HBr using a H from C1 to make one alkene, then using a H from C3 to make the other, and check if both are possible.
walkthrough:
**Recall what ethanolic KOH does**

Great start. Aqueous KOH gives substitution to an alcohol, but KOH in ethanol gives elimination. HBr is removed to form a C=C double bond.

$$\text{R-CHBr-CH}_2\text{-R'} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-CH=CH-R'} + \text{Br}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Look at the structure of 2-bromobutane**

Draw it out clearly so you can see your choices:

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

The Br is on C2. The carbons next door are C1 on the left and C3 on the right. Both have hydrogen atoms that can be removed.

**Form the two possible alkenes**

Remove H from C1 gives the terminal alkene, remove H from C3 gives the internal alkene.

$$\text{From C1: CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{HBr}$$
$$\text{From C3: CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3 + \text{HBr}$$

So both but-1-ene and but-2-ene form together.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ (but-2-ene) is one product, formed by removing H from C3, but it is not the only one. This choice forgets that H can also be removed from C1.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$ (but-1-ene) is one product, formed by removing H from C1, but it is not the only one. This choice forgets that H can also be removed from C3.
options.C: Correct. 2-bromobutane is unsymmetrical around C2, so elimination of HBr can happen in two directions to give both $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$.
options.D: Incorrect. While $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ is correct, $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH=CH}_2$ (buta-1,3-diene) cannot form here. Elimination removes only one HBr to give one double bond, not two, and there are not enough Br atoms for that.
